security_audit.summary: The markdown backtick findings are false positives caused by prompt text, code-fence parsing, and documentation formatting. The skill does handle OpenAI API credentials from configuration, environment variables, and application settings, and it generates runnable Python code that requires strict sandbox controls. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Community skill reads OpenAI credentials from environment and application settings.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent for credential use, use scoped keys, and avoid reading ambient secrets by default.

remediation.issue: The OpenAI base URL can come from configuration or environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict base_url to approved endpoints or warn users before sending credentials to non-default endpoints.

remediation.issue: The skill generates runnable Python code from user-controlled data context and requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Run generated scripts only in a locked sandbox with network, filesystem, and process limits.

content.value_statement: Raw datasets are hard to explain without clean analysis and charts. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code generate pandas workflows and styled visuals.
actual_capabilities: Generates Python scripts for data analysis tasks.
Uses pandas for cleaning, filtering, and aggregation workflows.
Creates Matplotlib and Seaborn chart code.
Applies a professional plotting theme through helper functions.
limitations: Requires a sandbox with pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn installed.
Generated code should be reviewed before execution on sensitive data.
The skill depends on an OpenAI-compatible model client.
It does not validate dataset quality or statistical assumptions automatically.

use_cases.title: Create report charts
use_cases.description: Turn a small business dataset into clear bar, line, scatter, pie, or heatmap visuals.

use_cases.title: Explore tabular data
use_cases.description: Generate pandas analysis steps that clean, group, and summarize structured data.

use_cases.title: Prepare presentation visuals
use_cases.description: Produce styled chart code that matches a professional report or slide deck.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this CSV data and create a short summary with one useful chart. Focus on the main trend and outliers.

prompt_templates.title: Compare categories
prompt_templates.prompt: Group the data by category, compare the main metric, and generate a professional bar chart with clear labels.

prompt_templates.title: Find relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore relationships between the numeric fields, identify strong patterns, and create the best visualization for the finding.

prompt_templates.title: Build a full analysis workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete analysis plan for this dataset, including cleaning, aggregation, validation checks, and two polished chart outputs.

output_examples.input: Sales data with region, month, revenue, and product category columns.
output_examples.output: A cleaned monthly revenue summary, a regional comparison chart, and notes about the strongest sales trend.

output_examples.input: Customer support data with ticket type, response time, priority, and status.
output_examples.output: A grouped response-time analysis, a priority heatmap, and a short explanation of operational bottlenecks.

output_examples.input: Marketing campaign data with channel, spend, conversions, and date.
output_examples.output: A channel performance summary, a conversion trend chart, and recommended metrics to review before publishing.

best_practices: Provide column names, data types, and a short goal before asking for analysis.
Review generated Python before running it on private or regulated datasets.
Run chart scripts in a restricted sandbox with clear file output limits.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets or personal data into analysis prompts.
Do not run generated code in an unrestricted local environment.
Do not treat generated charts as statistically valid without checking assumptions.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps generate Python analysis scripts and styled chart code for tabular datasets.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute Python code directly?
faq.answer: The skill generates code for sandbox execution. Users should run it only in a restricted environment.

faq.question: Which libraries does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn in the sandbox environment.

faq.question: Can it create presentation-ready charts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes helper styling for professional Matplotlib and Seaborn visualizations.

faq.question: What should users avoid?
faq.answer: Users should avoid sharing secrets, running generated scripts without review, or trusting results without validation.
